definition: A formal decision or arrangement between two or more parties.
example: According to the agreement, the project must be completed by December.

definition: A promise or guarantee that something is true or will happen.
example: The sales manager gave his assurance that the delivery would arrive on time.

definition: The act of stopping something that was previously planned or arranged.
example: The clause states that there is a fee for the cancellation of the service.

definition: To discover the facts or arrive at a conclusion or decision.
example: The investigation will determine who was responsible for the error.

definition: An arrangement to do something or a formal involvement in a task.
example: The consultant's engagement with the firm lasted for six months.

definition: To start or create an organization, system, or set of rules.
example: The two companies hope to establish a long-term business relationship.

definition: To force someone to do something because it is the law or a rule.
example: The contract obligates the tenant to pay the rent on the first of every month.

definition: A person or group of people involved in a legal agreement or dispute.
example: Both parties must sign the document for it to be legally binding.

definition: A specific condition or rule included within a legal document.
example: There is a special provision in the contract regarding overtime pay.

definition: To find an acceptable solution to a problem or difficulty.
example: The mediator helped both sides resolve their disagreement peacefully.

definition: To pull or draw someone's interest or attention toward something.
example: The new advertising campaign is designed to attract younger customers.

definition: To use up resources, or to buy and use goods and services.
example: Modern printers consume a large amount of electricity.

definition: To make someone believe that something is true or to persuade them.
example: It was difficult to convince the board to increase the marketing budget.

definition: At the present time; now.
example: We are currently reviewing our strategy for the upcoming fiscal year.

definition: Something that is very popular for a short period of time.
example: Market researchers need to tell the difference between a real trend and a fad.

definition: A sudden brilliant idea or a person/thing that motivates others.
example: The designer found inspiration for the logo in traditional Japanese art.

definition: To advertise or promote a product to a specific group of people.
example: The company decided to market the new beverage as a health drink.

definition: To make someone do something by giving them good reasons.
example: A good salesperson knows how to persuade customers to buy.

definition: To meet the needs, desires, or expectations of someone.
example: Our primary goal is to satisfy the requirements of our clients.

definition: Achieving or producing a lot of results or goods.
example: The morning meeting was very productive and we finished the plan early.

definition: A special quality or feature that makes someone or something different from others.
example: One characteristic of this laptop is its extremely long battery life.

definition: A result or effect of an action or condition, often an unpleasant one.
example: The consequence of failing to follow the instructions is a voided warranty.

definition: To think carefully about something, typically before making a decision.
example: Please consider all the terms and conditions before signing the document.

definition: To provide protection against loss, damage, or accidents.
example: Does this insurance policy cover water damage to the office equipment?

definition: The end of a period of time during which an agreement is official.
example: You should renew your subscription before the expiration date.

definition: Happening often or many times.
example: The software is updated frequently to fix minor bugs and security issues.

definition: To suggest something is true without saying it directly.
example: The high price of the product does not necessarily imply high quality.

definition: A statement telling someone that you will definitely do something.
example: The company failed to keep its promise to repair the machine for free.

definition: To keep someone or something safe from injury, damage, or loss.
example: The warranty is designed to protect the consumer from defective parts.

definition: The general opinion that people have about someone or something.
example: That manufacturer has a reputation for producing very reliable engines.

definition: To need something or make something necessary.
example: Most repairs require you to show your original receipt as proof of purchase.

definition: A number of different types of the same thing.
example: The store offers a wide variety of extended warranty plans.

definition: To give attention to or deal with a matter or problem.
example: The CEO will address the issue of falling sales at the next meeting.

definition: To stay away from someone or something, or prevent something from happening.
example: Careful planning helps the company avoid unnecessary risks.

definition: To show clearly that something exists or is true by giving proof.
example: We need to demonstrate that our new product is better than the competition.

definition: To grow or change into a more advanced or larger form.
example: The marketing team is working to develop a new brand identity.

definition: To judge or calculate the quality, importance, or value of something.
example: Management will evaluate the success of the project after six months.

definition: To collect several things together, often from different places or people.
example: We need to gather more information about our customers' spending habits.

definition: To ask someone if they would like to have something or if they would like you to do something.
example: The company decided to offer a discount to its most loyal clients.

definition: More important than anything else; main.
example: Our primary concern is the safety of our employees.

definition: The right or opportunity to use or see something.
example: You need a password to access the company's confidential files.

definition: To give something to be used for a particular purpose.
example: The IT department will allocate a new laptop to every new employee.

definition: Able to exist or work with something else without causing problems.
example: This software is not compatible with older operating systems.

definition: To remove something that has been written or stored on a computer.
example: Be careful not to delete any important documents by mistake.

definition: To show information in visual form on a screen.
example: The monitor can display high-resolution images and videos.

definition: To make an exact copy of something.
example: It is a good idea to duplicate your files on an external hard drive.

definition: A situation in which something does not work as it should.
example: A power failure caused the entire office network to shut down.

definition: To understand or find the solution to a problem after thinking about it.
example: We need to figure out why the printer is making a strange noise.

definition: To pay no attention to something or someone.
example: You should not ignore the system warning messages on your screen.

definition: To put a new program or piece of hardware onto a computer system.
example: I need to install the latest version of the antivirus software.

definition: A detailed list of all the goods or equipment in a particular place.
example: The store keeps an inventory of all its electronic components.

definition: A system of computers that are connected to share information.
example: Our office network allows us to share files quickly and easily.

definition: To allow something to happen or to allow someone to do something.
example: The security system will only permit authorized users to enter.

definition: A set of actions that is the official or right way of doing something.
example: The technician followed the standard procedure to fix the server.

definition: To take the place of something, or to put something new in the place of something old.
example: The company decided to replace all the old monitors with new ones.

definition: To find and bring back information from a computer's memory.
example: The technician managed to retrieve the data from the damaged disk.

definition: To look for information on a computer or on the internet.
example: You can search for the document by typing its name in the box.

definition: To stop a machine or computer from working by turning it off.
example: Please remember to shut down your computer before you leave.

definition: Relating to the practical use of machines, or science in industry.
example: If you have any technical problems, please call the help desk.

definition: To make something more modern by adding new information or features.
example: It is important to update your software regularly for security.
